title: Advancing rare disease therapeutics through digital twins: Opportunities in drug development and precision dosing

content.abstract_summary: Systematic review (16 studies from 49 identified) of digital twin (DT) implementations in rare disease (RD) drug development, analyzing PBPK, PopPK, QSP, physiome modeling, and combined approaches. Key finding: no published paper implements a true DT as defined by three criteria — (1) individual patient representation, (2) fusion of heterogeneous data sources, (3) real-time iterative updating. Current implementations are DT precursors, not full DTs. Reviews disease progression modeling, preclinical-to-FIH scaling, pediatric extrapolation, scarce-data scenarios, DDI modeling, and clinical accessibility. Forward-looking: generative AI (GANs, VAEs, diffusion models) and generative digital twins (GDTs) integrating spatial omics + mechanistic models as the next step. Use case: epidermolysis bullosa (EB). Saarland University, Saarbrücken (Lehr group).
key_findings: True DT definition (from authors): dynamic, continuously updateable computational representation of an individual patient, integrating mechanistic + empirical + population models with patient-specific real-world data — NONE of the 16 reviewed papers fully satisfy this definition because all lack real-time iterative updating

Three closest DT precursors: Susilo et al. (QSP for NHL mosunetuzumab — per-patient parameter estimation), Kaddi et al. (QSP/PBPK for Pompe disease — calibrated to individual patients), Yıldırım et al. (cardiovascular hemodynamic DT for congenital heart disease) — all fail the real-time updating criterion

FDA and EMA regulatory context: FDA CDER AI discussion paper describes DTs as a coming technology; EMA multi-annual AI workplan includes DT pilot studies in 2024 and 2026 — specific DT regulatory framework does not yet exist

Generative digital twins (GDTs): emerging concept integrating generative AI (spatial omics, multiplexed imaging, diffusion models, GANs) with mechanistic models — enables multi-scale DTs that reproduce tissue/organ-level phenotypes and can be interrogated causally ('what-if' simulations)

QSP model accepted as confirmatory FDA evidence: McBride et al. QSP model for rADAMTS13 in congenital TTP was submitted to and accepted by FDA as confirmatory evidence for rADAMTS131 efficacy over plasma — first QSP-for-regulatory-approval case

Key barriers for DT clinical adoption: data interoperability (FHIR, DICOM, OMOP not uniformly implemented), computational cost, interpretability/clinician trust, validation against clinical outcomes, ethical issues (federated learning, dynamic consent, patient data ownership)

Generative approaches for RD data augmentation: GANs, VAEs, diffusion models can generate synthetic yet biologically plausible datasets; ontology-enhanced or knowledge-guided versions improve biological consistency and fairness in underrepresented populations
limitations: 16 studies reviewed is a small sample — rare disease DT publications are too few for robust conclusions; findings reflect early-stage field, not mature technology

DT definition is stricter than many papers use — creates gap between authors' 'true DT' and what most publications call a DT; practical guidance for the field may be different from the strict theoretical definition

Generative DTs section is forward-looking with minimal empirical support — Wu & Koelzer reference is cited but not critically reviewed; actual performance of GDTs in rare disease settings not yet documented

extracted_claims.text: In general, all assessed manuscripts do not align with the DT definition stated [here] because they lack more than one of the following essential elements: (i) representation of an individual patient, (ii) fusion of heterogeneous data sources, and (iii) iterative updating via real-time data transfer.
FDA accepted the results from the QSP model as confirmative evidence proving the advantages of rADAMTS13 compared to plasma-based therapy.

GDTs integrate generative AI with omics and imaging-derived data, including spatial omics and multiplexed imaging, to create high-fidelity, spatially resolved virtual representations of biological systems.

numerical_findings.description: Systematic literature review scope: 16 included studies from 49 identified via PubMed search on digital twins in rare diseases

gaps_addressed: Provides the most rigorous definition of digital twin in the pharmacology context — anchors WG discussion so members do not conflate a population model with a true DT; the 'three criteria' framework is directly usable in the scoping paper

QSP model accepted as regulatory evidence (McBride et al. rADAMTS13 FDA case) is the most concrete cross-SIG (QSP×regulatory) example in the library — directly supports WG argument that mechanistic models enhance regulatory trust

Generative DT concept (GDTs) bridges generative_ai pillar and hybrid_foundations: integrating spatial omics + diffusion models + mechanistic QSP is the direction that extends beyond current neural-ODE pharmacokinetics work
